clue.text: PM out west gets firm with frisky animal

indicators.note: W is the abbreviation for west, and 'out' says that letter is removed from the name

parts.note: Gordon Brown was the British Prime Minister when this puzzle appeared
CO is the standard abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister takes a firm line with a lively beast in the American West.
explanation.walkthrough: The PM is Gordon Brown, Prime Minister when this appeared; 'out west' removes the abbreviation for west from his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronco is an unbroken wild horse of the American West, known for bucking.

clue.text: Boastful threat of support against trouble

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
V is short for versus, against
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Someone threatening to take a stand against difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a show of boldness meant to impress or intimidate, a boastful display of courage.

clue.text: Fruit that's all dead?

definitions.meaning: a small oval fruit grown around the Mediterranean
split as ..., nought alive, which is the same as everyone being dead

explanation.surface: A gloomy question about whether any fruit has survived.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second sense: O (nought) plus LIVE, nobody living.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is the small oily stone fruit of a Mediterranean evergreen tree.

clue.text: Some cut material for dress

indicators.note: turned into raw material and remade, so the letters of the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A piece of cloth trimmed to make a frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' rearranges SOME and CUT; 'for' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Costume is clothing, especially a particular style of dress or outfit for a role.

clue.text: Aim to get a sprout

parts.note: spire is an old word for a young shoot or sprout of a plant

explanation.surface: Advice to a gardener on how to grow a shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: To aim at something is to strive or hope for it, the verb's ambitious sense.

clue.text: Winter transport sounds murder

indicators.note: the clue says the word sounds like another when said

parts.note: to slay is to kill, murder

explanation.surface: A ghostly sleigh ride in winter gives off murderous noises.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleigh is a sledge pulled by horses or reindeer over snow.

clue.text: One's about to act in due course — their priorities are inappropriate

indicators.note: about means around, so the first letters go around the rest

parts.note: One is I, and 's makes IS
to do is to act
in due course means later, eventually

explanation.surface: Someone promising to act in time while their priorities are all wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' reads as I plus the 's turned into IS, and 'about' puts the rest between those two letters. The definition is a cryptic description of idol worshippers.
explanation.definitionFit: Idol worshippers put false gods first, so their sense of what matters most is misplaced.

clue.text: English allow people in — perhaps into a compound

indicators.note: the people go inside the allow word

parts.note: to let is to allow
men means people

explanation.surface: England opens its doors to newcomers, perhaps into a fenced enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like an enclosed camp; it is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemical elements combine to form compounds, so an element is what may go into one.

clue.text: It's a job for a librarian to limit noise

definitions.text: It's a job for a librarian to limit noise

parts.words: It's a job for a librarian to limit noise
parts.note: a librarian manages books and keeps a quiet room, so the phrase reads as both managing tomes and turning the sound down

explanation.surface: Keeping the library quiet is part of the librarian's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Volume means both a book and loudness: a librarian keeps volumes in order and keeps noise down.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the knob or setting that adjusts loudness, read jokily as managing books.

clue.text: Painter with 7s of Daedalian artistry

indicators.note: 7-down's answer means a component, so the painter's name is made from components of the following words

explanation.surface: An artist whose work shows the inventive genius of Daedalus.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 7 gives 'elements of': four consecutive letters inside 'Daedalian' give the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dali was the Spanish surrealist painter famous for melting clocks.

clue.text: Spooks get energy dancing in a country churchyard

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Ghosts gain energy and dance among the graves of a village churchyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges SPOOKS, GET and E. STOKE POGES, in Buckinghamshire, is the churchyard of Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Its churchyard is traditionally held to be the setting of Thomas Gray's famous elegy.

clue.text: Water pistol first takes the cake

indicators.note: 'pistol first' tells you the gun word comes before the water word

parts.note: gat is old American slang for a gun
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: Someone with a water pistol wins the prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the cake' is an idiom for winning; here 'takes' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich, elaborate cake, from the French word for one.

clue.text: Possible anger with dud exam result?

definitions.note: the definition is adjectival: describing an exam that got no result

indicators.note: a possible version of the letters is one way they might be arranged

explanation.surface: A failed exam may well lead to anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible' rearranges ANGER and DUD; the question mark admits the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper left without a grade has, in a sense, no mark given as its outcome.

clue.text: The way it measures …

parts.note: read literally from Greek: hodos means way, and the device is a measurer of the way travelled

explanation.surface: Someone describing the method by which a thing is measured.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis leads into the next clue, about distance. Greek hodos, a road or way, plus a meter makes an instrument that measures distance travelled.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument records the distance covered by a wheeled vehicle, like a mileage counter.

clue.text: Traditional fate for stray offspring perhaps — hang with a rope …

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible version, so the letters of the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grim suggestion that lost children were once hanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges HANG and A ROPE. The ellipsis joins the clue to the next, offering mercy as an alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: Children without parents traditionally ended up in a home for them, run by charity or parish.

clue.text: … distance reported for accomplishment

indicators.note: reported speech is what is said, so the word sounds like the one spelt

parts.note: feet are a unit of length, so a distance can be measured in them

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, distance covered is announced as an achievement.
explanation.definitionFit: A feat is a notable deed or achievement, often one needing skill or strength.

clue.text: Fuzz curtailed arboreal area

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a copse is a small wood, an area of trees

explanation.surface: Bushy growth cut back in a wooded area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuzz' is slang for the police, not a fluffy texture.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuzz is old slang for the police, and cops are police officers.

clue.text: … or merciful 7 with new opening

indicators.note: the first letter is replaced by a different one

parts.note: the cross-reference is to 7-down, a component or constituent

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: or perhaps a merciful sentence starts things afresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with new opening' swaps the first letter of 7-down for C.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement means lenient and showing mercy, as of a judge or of mild weather.

clue.text: Singular past fashion for assault on 16?

parts.note: the cross-reference is to the police; a British police officer is nicknamed a bobby
to sock someone is to punch them, an assault on them

explanation.surface: An old fashion craze recast as an attack on the police.
explanation.walkthrough: To sock a bobby is to assault a policeman. 'Singular' because the item is usually worn and named in pairs, as bobby socks: ankle socks worn by 1940s-50s teenage girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobby socks were the turned-down ankle socks fashionable among American teenagers in the 1940s and 1950s.

clue.text: Good purposes for bankers' sweeteners?

parts.note: bon is French for good
uses are purposes, functions

explanation.surface: Asking whether bankers' payouts serve worthy ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonuses are extra payments on top of salary, notoriously large for bankers.

clue.text: Room to keep horse in Sussex resort

indicators.note: the resort holds the letter inside it

parts.note: Camber, with Camber Sands, is a seaside resort in East Sussex, southern England
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: Finding space to stable a horse at a seaside town in Sussex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' looks like an animal; in crosswords it is slang for heroin, H.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is a room, especially a private or formal one.

clue.text: Go to live in Ribblesdale

definitions.meaning: to make a new home somewhere
A market town in Ribblesdale, North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Moving to a dale in the Yorkshire countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Ribblesdale is the valley of the River Ribble in northern England; Settle is its main town.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle is to make one's permanent home in a place.

clue.text: Yorkist insurgent in depression going to the dogs

indicators.note: the rebel is placed inside the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a hollow, a depression in a surface
Jack Cade led the 1450 Kentish rebellion and was linked with the Yorkist cause

explanation.surface: A rebel for the House of York finds himself in a slump, with everything falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the dogs means declining in morals or standards, which is what a decadent society is doing.

clue.text: Grandmother keeps funny hat for prophet

indicators.note: the grandmother word keeps the other letters inside it

parts.note: nan is a familiar British word for a grandmother

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters of the word hat are jumbled

explanation.surface: Granny holds on to a silly hat that suits a seer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' signals the hat is jumbled; nan is everyday British for a grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathan was the Old Testament prophet who rebuked King David over Bathsheba.

clue.text: Distributor charges for energy, including light

indicators.note: the words include the answer within them, running across the gap

explanation.surface: An energy supplier's bills, light included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for energy' belongs to the surface only; the letters run across 'Distributor charges'.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a portable light, what Americans call a flashlight.

clue.text: Editors can make them

indicators.note: the letters of the first two words can be made into the plural noun the clue describes

explanation.surface: A remark about the cuts that editors are able to make.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange EDITORS and CAN; the whole clue is also a fair description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Redactions are edits or cuts made to a text, the work an editor does.

clue.text: Stone that killed Oswald

definitions.meaning: Jack ... shot Lee Harvey Oswald, the assassin of President Kennedy, in 1963

explanation.surface: A stone that seems to have been a murder weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone' tempts you towards a missile that killed someone; it is a gem, and the killer is the man who shot Oswald.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruby is a red gemstone, a variety of corundum; Jack Ruby was the nightclub owner who shot Oswald.

clue.text: Having a motif off Alexandria?

definitions.meaning: built around a particular subject or idea
Alexandria lies on the coast of the Mediterranean, so waters off it are in the Med

explanation.surface: Something decorated with a recurring pattern found near an Egyptian port.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, THE MED, for the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something organised around a recurring subject or idea is described as having a theme.

clue.text: Cheers for an artist of deception

indicators.note: a thin anagram signal: the letters of the word are exchanged for a new order

explanation.surface: Raising a toast to a painter of optical illusions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' signals an exchange of letters: CHEERS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: M. C. Escher was the Dutch graphic artist famous for impossible staircases and optical illusions.
